heard: an interstellar visitor sped up as it left without venting a tail. On October 19, 2017, the Pan-SDARS telescope in Hawaii discovered the object named Aumuamua. Astronomers found a reddish, highly elongated body with an estimated length of roughly 400 meters. Observations revealed a length-to-width ratio of approximately 10 to 1 as its brightness varied by a factor of 10. Even when closest to the sun, it showed zero signs of a coma, dust cloud, or tail. Harvard astrophysicist Avi Loeb proposed the tumbling object could be an artificial light sail. While a 2023 theory points to invisible hydrogen gas venting from water ice, an interstellar visitor left without a tail.
